An **eval suite** is a set of inputs with expected results for one agent. You run it like a test suite, pin today's score as the **baseline**, and the API answers **HTTP 422** when a later run scores lower. Everything here is on the REST API the dashboard uses; the exhaustive list is in the [REST API](/docs/reference/api/).

<BudgetEvalGate client:visible />

## Suites

A suite is a named list of cases. A case has a `name`, an `input` string, and an `expected` string and/or an `assert` object. Suites are upserted by `(tenant, agent, name)`.

PAL stores `expected` and `assert` with the case. Your runner (or `pal test`) decides pass or fail and reports `passed` and `score` per case. The one assertion the server checks itself is `{"grounded":true}`, which forces a case to fail when the output claims an action nothing backed.

```http
POST /v1/eval-suites
{
  "agentName": "research-agent",
  "name": "factual-accuracy",
  "cases": [
    { "name": "case-1", "input": "What year did WWII end?",
      "expected": "1945", "assert": { "contains": "1945" } }
  ]
}
```

Also `GET /v1/eval-suites` (optionally `?agentName=`), `GET /v1/eval-suites/{id}` and `DELETE /v1/eval-suites/{id}`.

## Recording a run and the CI gate

Run the agent on each case yourself, or use `pal test`, which waits for each run to finish (`--timeout` caps the wait, default 2m). Then post the per-case results. The server computes the score (mean of case scores) and compares it with the pinned baseline for the same agent and branch. A score more than 0.01 below the baseline returns **422**, which fails a CI step. With no baseline pinned, nothing regresses.

```http
POST /v1/eval-runs
{
  "suiteId": "suite-uuid", "agentVersion": "v2", "commitSha": "abc1234", "branch": "main",
  "caseResults": [ { "name": "case-1", "passed": true, "score": 0.95, "actual": "1945" } ]
}

200 OK
{ "id": "run-uuid", "passed": true, "score": 0.95, "regressed": false, "baselineScore": 0.94 }

422 Unprocessable Entity   (regressed against the baseline)
{ "id": "run-uuid", "score": 0.91, "regressed": true, "baselineScore": 0.94 }
```

List runs with `GET /v1/eval-runs?suiteId=&agentName=&branch=`. A full pipeline (run, post, stop on 422, deploy, receipt) is in [Examples](/docs/start/examples/).

## Baselines

Pin an eval run as the baseline for an agent and branch; later runs on that branch are compared against it.

```bash
pal test --agent research-agent --suite factual-accuracy --set-baseline   # run, then pin this run
```

Over REST, `POST /v1/eval-baselines` with `{ "agentName", "branch", "evalRunId" }` pins one, and `GET /v1/eval-baselines?agentName=&branch=` reads it (404 `{"error":"no baseline"}` when unset).

## Reading the history

Two read-only endpoints over existing `eval_runs` data feed the dashboard's quality-trend sparkline and top-failing-cases view.

| Endpoint | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /v1/eval-observability/failures?agentName=&branch=&limit=` | `clusters`: failing cases grouped across recent runs, worst first (`case`, `failures`, `seen`, `failRate`, `sampleError`, `firstSeen`, `lastSeen`), and `runsScanned`. `limit` is the number of runs scanned (default 50, cap 200) |
| `GET /v1/eval-observability/trends?agentName=&branch=&limit=` | `points`, oldest first (`runId`, `createdAt`, `score`, `passRate`, `passed`, `costUsd`, `agentVersion`, `commitSha`), plus `latestVsMean` and `regressing` (the latest score is below the mean of earlier ones) |

## Human feedback and rehearsals

Collect reactions on individual runs. Score is 1 to 5; 4 to 5 is positive, 1 to 2 is negative.

```http
POST /v1/runs/{id}/feedback
{ "score": 2, "comment": "The agent missed the follow-up question",
  "preferredOutput": "It should have asked for clarification first" }
```

`GET /v1/runs/{id}/feedback` lists a run's history; `GET /v1/agents/{name}/feedback` returns the aggregate (`totalFeedback`, `avgScore`, `thumbsUp`, `thumbsDown`, `last7DaysAvgScore`).

**Rehearsals** pull past failed runs and runs scored 2 or lower as synthetic test cases, so you can replay them against a candidate version before you flip traffic. The endpoint returns the cases; `pal test --rehearse` runs them.

```http
POST /v1/runs/rehearse
{ "agentName": "research-agent", "window": "7d", "limit": 20,
  "includeFailures": true, "includeLowScore": true }
```

Defaults: `window` 7d, `limit` 25 (max 200), both `include*` flags true.

## A/B experiments

An experiment records scores for two agent versions and can promote the winner. `PickVariant` implements a deterministic FNV-1a split, but nothing in the run path calls it, so **experiments do not route traffic today**. You assign variants yourself and `record` each outcome.

```http
POST /v1/experiments
{ "agentName": "research-agent", "name": "prompt-v2-test",
  "variantAVersion": "v1", "variantBVersion": "v2",
  "trafficSplitB": 20, "autoPromote": true, "minRunsToPromote": 100 }

POST /v1/experiments/{id}/record      { "variant": "b", "score": 0.95 }     # running mean per variant
POST /v1/experiments/{id}/conclude    { "winner": "b", "promote": true }    # "a" | "b" | "tie"
```

`trafficSplitB` is stored, not applied. With `autoPromote` on, PAL promotes the leader once both arms have at least `minRunsToPromote` runs (default 100) and one leads by more than 0.02. That is a fixed margin, not a significance test. `GET /v1/experiments` and `GET /v1/experiments/{id}` list and read them.

Span attributes and traces: [Observability](/docs/observability/).

## CI gates for your agent repo

`pal ci init` writes a GitHub Actions workflow and a generic `.pal/ci.sh` that run, in order,
manifest lint, a policy/security lint, the hermetic eval suite with the baseline regression gate,
and a budget check. All pass/fail decisions are deterministic code; a model never grades the gate.
The run writes `pal-ci-report.json` and a PR comment.

```bash
pal ci init --suite ci --dry-run   # preview the files
pal ci init --suite ci             # write them
pal ci lint                        # the two offline gates, no credentials
```

Set the repo secret `PAL_API_KEY` and variables `PAL_API_URL` and `PAL_CI_STAGING_ACK=1`. The key
must belong to a **staging** workspace: the gate deploys the PR's manifest there before evaluating it.
